title: Federal prosecutors arrest California CEO over $300M Nvidia AI chip smuggling scheme
subtitle: Greg Lui, head of Earthmade Computer, is accused of routing H100 and A100 servers to China through Malaysia and Singapore between 2023 and 2024 — part of an enforcement pattern that now spans more than $800 million in diverted hardware.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Federal agents arrested 38-year-old Greg Lui, owner of California-based Earthmade Computer, on October 1 and charged him with conspiring to ship servers containing more than $300 million worth of restricted Nvidia AI chips to buyers in China. The indictment names the Nvidia A100 and H100 data-center GPUs and the PNY GeForce RTX 4090 and 5090 — all classified under ECCN 4A090.a, which requires a US license for export to China. Prosecutors say Lui worked with unidentified co-conspirators from 2023 to 2024 and routed shipments through Malaysia and Singapore to obscure the end destination. He faces charges of conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act, outbound smuggling, and conspiracy to commit money laundering, carrying more than 20 years of potential prison exposure.

The arrest is not isolated. Combined with the March case against a co-founder of Super Micro Computer — accused of diverting roughly $510 million in Nvidia hardware — US enforcement has now publicly accounted for more than $800 million in restricted chips that reached China through third-country transshipment. Senators Jim Banks and Elizabeth Warren have already written to the Commerce Department asking for a review of Nvidia's export licenses in light of the pattern, and Nvidia says it has strengthened its own controls. The through-line of the two cases is that the chips did not leak out through porous ports; they moved through documented freight forwarders with falsified end-user paperwork.

What this exposes is the real shape of the export-control regime. On paper, the H100 is one of the most tightly controlled products in modern electronics. In practice, a small corporate shell with the right customer relationships can move nine-figure quantities before enforcement catches up. The policy debate for the next year will be whether the US tightens the transshipment loopholes — new rules on freight brokers, mandatory end-user verification, hardware-level attestations tying a chip to its licensed buyer — or whether Washington accepts a baseline level of leakage as the cost of keeping Nvidia's compliant export business running.

A note for learners interested in AI policy or chip-industry careers: the compliance layer around frontier compute is becoming its own technical specialty. Hardware attestation, cryptographic chip identity, secure supply-chain tracking — these are not abstract policy ideas anymore; they are things semiconductor firms are being asked to build. If you are in computer engineering or infosec, the intersection of export control, cryptographic attestation and GPU firmware is a hiring area that did not exist two years ago. The Lui case is the kind of enforcement that creates permanent demand for people who can prove, at the silicon level, where a chip actually ended up.
